maria_perf: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak merged this morning, host-side CPU for token parsing spiked ~18% on streaming gRPC ingress :eyes:

sam_runtime: saw the same. traces point to parse_frame + small write churn in the chunker.

liz_eng: any specific payloads? small chat messages or long-context?

maria_perf: mostly short prompts (<=128 tokens) during canary. CPU per-request went from ~12ms -> ~14.2ms on host preproc.

sam_runtime: profile snippet from canary node:
```
parse_frame          42.1%
buffer_copy          31.8%
grpc_writev_overhead 12.3%
kv_lookup             8.4%
serialize             5.6%
```

jonah_sre: grpc_writev_overhead that high screams inefficient coalescing / lots of tiny buffers hitting kernel.

liz_eng: could be our framed-chunk size heuristic. we recently lowered the target chunk to <512B to reduce latency for tiny responses — maybe we regressed tail CPU.

sam_runtime: hypothesis: new kernel selector prefers a compact attention kernel that reduces GPU time but increases host pre-serialize steps (extra buffer ops). it changes the callsite shape for streaming code paths which disables our fast-path coalesce.

maria_perf: reproducer command: `make bench-stream-chunk PAYLOAD=short COUNT=10000` — results attached in CI.

sam_runtime: tried locally, can reproduce ~+16% host CPU on my devbox. quick hack: re-enable coalesce when `expected_response_bytes < 2KB`. that drops buffer_copy down ~9%.

liz_eng: nice. can we make that a runtime policy instead of an absolute chunk size? maybe factor in `kernel_choice == compact` to keep trailing-write batching.

sam_runtime: yeah I'll sketch a policy: prefer coalesce if (kernel == compact && median_response < 2KB) OR (p50_latency_target < 50ms).

jonah_sre: also saw increased number of syscalls in the canary trace: `writev` calls per req jumped x3. if we gate around writev we should reduce syscall overhead.

sam_runtime: patch in flight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3421 — adds `stream_coalesce_policy` and a small metric `host.writev_per_request`.

maria_perf: local bench after patch: host CPU back to +2% vs baseline and writev_per_request from 3.2 -> 1.1. can we run a canary with ~5% traffic?

liz_eng: I'll coordinate canary. rolling a canary now via infra console.

ci-bot: deploy started for canary group (tag: pr-3421) — 5% of us-west streaming traffic.

sam_runtime: also adding a tiny optimization: delay parsing until first non-empty chunk arrives (avoid parse_frame for keepalive-only handshakes). small wins in p95.

maria_perf: thanks. follow-up: collect `host.parse_frame_ms` histogram and `host.writev_per_request` for next 2 hours. if anything >10% regression we auto-revert.

jonah_sre: noted. I'll set alerts.

liz_eng: if canary looks good, we'll land policy behind `optimize.coalesce=true` flag and schedule a perf postmortem doc with before/after traces.

sam_runtime: assigning follow-ups: @sam_runtime handle PR + metric; @liz_eng run canary & roll; @maria_perf validate long-tail perf.

maria_perf: ack. will post a short summary once we have 30m of canary data. :rocket:
